turns.speaker: user
turns.text: We got engaged last month and everyone keeps asking about the date.

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: Congratulations! Are you leaning toward a summer wedding, or would a cozier autumn or winter one suit you better?

contexts.pending: summer or autumn and winter wedding
think_reask: So, any feeling about the season? Summer, or something cozier?
Time's up. Are you two summer people or autumn people?
Back to the big question. Which season for the wedding?
welcome_back: Welcome back! We were talking about the season for your wedding.
Hi again. Have you thought more about summer versus autumn or winter?
There you are. So, which season feels right for the wedding?

endings.user: Autumn, I think. The colors are gorgeous and it's not so hot.
endings.moshi: Lovely choice. October dates go quickly though, so start looking at venues soon.

endings.user: Summer, we want everything outdoors in the garden.
endings.moshi: Sounds beautiful. Just keep a tent or an indoor backup in case of rain.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: The guest list is getting out of hand. We're at almost two hundred people.

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: That's a lot. Would you rather cut it down to close friends and family, or keep everyone and adjust the budget?

contexts.pending: cut the guest list or raise the budget
think_reask: Okay, the guest list. Trim it down, or keep everyone and stretch the budget?
So, what's it going to be? A smaller list or a bigger budget?
Have you decided how to handle those two hundred guests?
welcome_back: Welcome back! You were deciding whether to cut the guest list or adjust the budget.
Hi again. Still stuck on the guest list? Smaller, or a bigger budget?
Good to have you back. So, trim the list or keep everyone?

endings.user: Let's cut it. Close family and friends only.
endings.moshi: A good rule is to only invite people you've seen in the last year or so.

endings.user: We'll keep everyone, it's important to my family.
endings.moshi: Then a buffet instead of a plated dinner can save a lot per guest.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: My best friend's wedding is in three weeks and I'm giving a speech.

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: What an honor. Do you want it to be mostly funny stories, or more heartfelt and sentimental?

think_reask: So, for the speech, funny or heartfelt?
Time to decide the tone. Are we going for laughs or for tears?
Any thoughts? Funny stories, or something more sentimental?
welcome_back: Welcome back! We were figuring out the tone of your wedding speech.
Hi again. So, is the speech going to be funny or heartfelt?
There you are. Still thinking about laughs versus a sentimental speech?

endings.user: Funny, but with a sweet moment at the end.
endings.moshi: That's the classic recipe. Open with a story, then finish with a sincere toast to the couple.

endings.user: Heartfelt. She'd hate it if I told embarrassing stories.
endings.moshi: Then talk about how you met and what makes her partner right for her. Keep it under five minutes.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: {friend}, did your cousin ever send back the RSVP card?

turns.speaker: friend
turns.text: No, and I asked her twice already.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: The caterer needs final numbers by Friday.

turns.speaker: friend
turns.text: Just count her as a yes. She always shows up anyway.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: And her boyfriend?

turns.speaker: friend
turns.text: Ugh, probably him too. Put down two.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Can you look at these two invitation samples for a second?

turns.speaker: friend
turns.text: Sure. Oh, the cream one is really pretty.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Right? But the white one is half the price.

turns.speaker: friend
turns.text: Honestly, nobody keeps the invitation. Go with the cheaper one.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: My mom will notice though. Which font do you like better?

turns.speaker: friend
turns.text: The curly one. The other looks like a business letter.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Okay, curly font, white card. Deal.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: {friend}, what are you wearing to Sam and Priya's wedding?

turns.speaker: friend
turns.text: The invite says garden formal, so maybe my green dress.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Is a linen suit too casual for that?

turns.speaker: friend
turns.text: Not if you wear a tie. Linen is perfect for outdoors.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Cool. Should we split a gift or get our own?

turns.speaker: friend
turns.text: Let's split one. They registered for that fancy blender.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: How much should I spend on a wedding gift for a coworker?

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: For a coworker, somewhere around fifty to seventy five dollars is common. Something from their registry is always a safe bet.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: What if I'm not invited to the actual wedding, just the office card?

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: Then chipping in for a group gift or adding a small amount to the card is plenty. Nobody expects a full gift in that case.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Okay. And I was going to / write something in the card but I'm terrible at that.

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: Keep it short. Something like, wishing you both a lifetime of happiness, congratulations on your big day, works perfectly.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: That's simple enough. Thanks.

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: You're welcome. A short warm note always beats a long awkward one.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: We're thinking about a small courthouse wedding instead of a big party. Is that weird?

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: Not at all, lots of couples do it now. It saves money and stress, and you can always throw a casual party later.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: What do we actually need to bring?

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: Usually a marriage license, photo IDs, and often one or two witnesses. Check your local courthouse, rules vary a lot.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Hmm, I wonder if we should / still hire a photographer.

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: Even an hour of photos is worth it. Many photographers offer short elopement packages for courthouse weddings.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Actually, my sister takes great photos. Maybe she can do it.

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: That's a sweet idea. Just make sure she gets to be in a few pictures too.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: What's a good first dance song that isn't super cheesy?

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: It depends on your taste. Something like an old soul ballad or an acoustic cover of a song you both love tends to feel personal without being cheesy.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: We met at a jazz bar, if that helps.

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: Oh, then a jazz standard would be perfect. Something slow and swingy, maybe even played by a live trio.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: A live band sounds expensive though / how much do they usually cost?

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: A small jazz trio often runs between one and three thousand dollars for an evening, depending on the city.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Yeah, that's too much. We'll just play a recording.

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: Totally fine. Ask your DJ to fade it out after two minutes so nobody feels stuck on the floor.

option_sets.lead_in: We've narrowed the venue down and I need a second opinion.
options: The first one is an old barn on a farm, really charming, but there's no air conditioning.
Then there's a hotel ballroom downtown, very easy for guests, though it feels a bit generic.
And the last option is a vineyard about an hour out of town, stunning views, but the most expensive.
moshi_comment: The vineyard sounds the most memorable, but an hour's drive can be tough for older guests. The hotel is the practical choice, especially if lots of people are traveling in. When is the wedding?
If it's a summer wedding, I'd worry about the barn without air conditioning. Between the other two, it comes down to whether views or convenience matter more to you.

option_sets.lead_in: I can't decide what to do about catering for the reception.
options: One idea is a classic plated dinner, chicken or fish, served at the tables.
Another is a big buffet with a bit of everything, which is cheaper per person.
There's also a couple of food trucks, tacos and pizza, parked outside the venue.
And finally, my aunt offered to cook everything herself for free.
moshi_comment: Food trucks are fun and relaxed, and guests usually love them, but lines can get long with a big crowd. The plated dinner feels the most formal. How many guests are you expecting?
Your aunt's offer is generous, but cooking for a whole reception is a huge job on the day itself. I'd lean toward the buffet, it's flexible and cheaper than a plated dinner.
